title: Failed flush requeues older messages behind newly enqueued messages
reasoning: flushPendingMessages drains a snapshot of pending messages, then awaits storeTranscriptEntry per entry. If new retry messages are enqueued while the await is pending and a later store fails, requeuePending appends the unflushed older snapshot entries to the tail of the live queue. A later flush can then persist newer messages before older failed messages, corrupting transcript ordering under an async failure interleaving.
recommendation: Requeue failed snapshot entries ahead of any messages that arrived during the flush, or serialize flush/enqueue ordering with an in-flight buffer so older drained entries retain priority after retry.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests are included, and this requires a storeTranscriptEntry mock that yields to allow enqueueing during an in-flight flush before throwing.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that starts a flush with two pending user messages, lets the second store call yield, enqueues a third message before the second call rejects, then verifies the next flush persists the second message before the third.
minimumFixScope: Adjust queue reinsert semantics or pending flush synchronization for the pending transcript queues, with a focused async ordering regression test.
